body: Three specific problems. (1) Template residue: FR-001 requires 'outcome, predictors, covariates' and an assumption disclaims 'post-task anxiety/rumination variables' — neither construct exists in the GateMem setup described anywhere else in this spec; these are verbatim leftovers from an unrelated (psychological/clinical) spec template and make FR-001 unimplementable as written. (2) Baseline asymmetry: SC-001 measures Access Control only against 'Retrieval-only' and SC-002 measures Utility only against 'Long-Context'. If each metric is compared against a different, single baseline, the central claim — that the gatekeeper resolves the leakage/utility trade-off better than integrated baselines — is not established; a method could look good on leakage versus one baseline and on utility versus another without dominating either. Each metric should be reported against both baselines. (3) Statistical design: FR-005 mandates an LMM with 'Domain' as random intercept, but the dataset has exactly four domains (medical, office, education, household); a random intercept estimated from four levels is unreliable, and the spec's own fallback (domain-stratified analysis) is likely to be the operative path. The assumption section acknowledges a power limitation but does not address the four-level random-effect issue specifically. Additionally, the assumption that a Llama-3-8B 'Long-Context' baseline runs on a GitHub Actions free-tier CPU-only runner is not established anywhere in the artifact; if it cannot, the cost-profiling comparison (SC-003) has no valid control.
